'''Joris van der Hoeven''' (born 1971) is a Dutch mathematician and computer scientist, specializing in [[algebraic analysis]] and [[computer algebra]]. He is the primary developer of [[GNU TeXmacs]].

==Education and career==
Joris van der Hoeven received in 1997 his doctorate from [[Paris Diderot University]] (Paris 7) with thesis ''Asymptotique automatique''.<ref>{{MathGenealogyProject | id = 98813}}</ref> He is a [[List of academic ranks#France|''Directeur de recherche'']] at the [[CNRS]] and head of the team ''Max Modélisation algébrique'' at the Laboratoire d'informatique of the [[École Polytechnique]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Joris van der Hoeven|website=TeXmacs|url=http://www.texmacs.org/joris/main/joris.html}}</ref>

==Research==
His research deals with [[transseries]] (''i.e.'' generalizations of [[formal power series]]) with applications to algebraic analysis and asymptotic solutions of [[Nonlinear_system#Nonlinear_differential_equations|nonlinear differential equations]]. In addition to transseries' properties as part of [[differential algebra]] and [[model theory]], he also examines their algorithmic aspects as well as those of classical complex function theory.

He is the main developer of [[GNU TeXmacs]] (a free scientific editing platform)<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.texmacs.org/tmweb/home/welcome.en.html|title=Welcome to GNU TeXmacs (FSF GNU project)|website=www.texmacs.org}}</ref> and Mathemagix (free software, a computer algebra and analysis system).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mathemagix.org/www/mmdoc/doc/html/main/index.en.html|title=Welcome to Mathemagix|website=www.mathemagix.org}}</ref>

In 2019, van der Hoeven and his coauthor David Harvey announced their discovery of the fastest known [[multiplication algorithm]], allowing the multiplication of <math>n</math>-bit [[binary number]]s in time <math>O(n\log n)</math>.<ref>{{Cite magazine|url=https://www.quantamagazine.org/mathematicians-discover-the-perfect-way-to-multiply-20190411/|title=Mathematicians Discover the Perfect Way to Multiply|last=Hartnett|first=Kevin|magazine=Quanta Magazine|date=11 April 2019|access-date=2019-05-03}}</ref> Their paper was [[peer review]]ed and published in the ''[[Annals of Mathematics]]'' in 2021.

==Recognition==
In 2018, he was an Invited Speaker (with [[Matthias Aschenbrenner]] and [[Lou van den Dries]]) with the talk ''On numbers, germs, and transseries'' at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]].<ref>{{cite arXiv|author=Aschenbrenner, M.|author2=van den Dries, L.|author3=van der Hoeven, J.|title=On numbers, germs, and transseries|year=2017|eprint=1711.06936|class=math.LO}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.mathunion.org/icm-plenary-and-invited-speakers|title=ICM Plenary and Invited Speakers|author=<!--Not stated-->|publisher=[[International Mathematical Union]]|access-date=May 12, 2020}}</ref> In 2018, the three received the [[Karp Prize]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/karp-prize-recipients/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190722150030/https://aslonline.org/asl-information/prizes-and-awards/karp-prize-recipients/ |archive-date=July 22, 2019 |url-status=live|title=Karp Prize Recipients|author=<!--Not stated-->|work=Association for Symbolic Logic |publisher=[[Association for Symbolic Logic]]|access-date=January 27, 2020}}</ref>
In 2022, he received the N. G. de Bruijn prize<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.wiskgenoot.nl/index.php?page=87&sid=2 |title=N.G. de Bruijn Prize |year=2024}}</ref>
